problem: With L = πDn as the total wire length, θ = T L/(GJ) is the total twist of all active coils, not 'the twist of one coil'. The next line δ = Rθ uses total twist, so the wording makes the derivation inconsistent.
fix: Say: 'The total twist over all active coils is θ = T L/(GJ) with L = πDn, and δ = Rθ.' Or, per coil: θ₁ = T(πD)/(GJ) and δ = nRθ₁.

problem: The sentence 'The component in the coil plane twists ... normal to the coil plane bends' is reversed relative to the formulas. At α=0 the axial load is normal to the coil plane and causes torsion, not bending; the component along the wire axis causes the bending M=WR sinα.
fix: Write: 'The component of W perpendicular to the wire axis produces torsion T=WR cosα; the component along the wire axis produces bending M=WR sinα.'

problem: Counting total coils instead of active coils makes n larger, so it overestimates δ and makes the spring seem softer (lower k), not stiffer. This also contradicts Quiz Q6.
fix: Say: 'Counting total coils instead of active coils overestimates deflection and makes the spring seem softer; end coils that do not deform must be excluded.'
